photoobj_basic.name: photoobj_basic
photoobj_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  run,
  rerun,
  field,
  mode,
  type,
  clean,
  flags,
  rowc,
  colc,
  cmodelmag_u,
  cmodelmag_g,
  cmodelmag_r,
  u,
  g,
  r,
  i,
  z,
  ra,
  dec,
  b,
  l,
  extinction_r,
  mjd,
  loadversion
FROM photoobj

params.description: Provides one-row-per-astronomical-object photometric and positional basic attributes from the photoobj table (pointing-level/basic object properties).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve basic photometry, positions, and metadata for a single object (by objid) or a set of objects. | Filter objects by photometric values, position (ra/dec), field/run/rerun, or quality flags. | Compose catalog-level selections (e.g., build color cuts, select by extinction or mjd) before joining to spectra or neighbor/aggregation tables. | Use as the photometric base when joining each object to one row per object (e.g., attach latest spectrum or aggregated neighbor counts) while preserving one-row-per-object semantics.
params.output_schema: objid: unique object identifier — from photoobj.objid | run: imaging run number — from photoobj.run | rerun: reduction pipeline rerun identifier — from photoobj.rerun | field: imaging field number — from photoobj.field | mode: imaging mode code — from photoobj.mode | type: object type code (e.g., star/galaxy) — from photoobj.type | clean: clean flag (quality indicator) — from photoobj.clean | flags: detection/processing flags bitmask — from photoobj.flags | rowc: centroid row coordinate in CCD pixels — from photoobj.rowc | colc: centroid column coordinate in CCD pixels — from photoobj.colc | cmodelmag_u: composite model magnitude in u band — from photoobj.cmodelmag_u | cmodelmag_g: composite model magnitude in g band — from photoobj.cmodelmag_g | cmodelmag_r: composite model magnitude in r band — from photoobj.cmodelmag_r | u: PSF/aperture (?) magnitude in u band as stored — from photoobj.u | g: PSF/aperture (?) magnitude in g band as stored — from photoobj.g | r: PSF/aperture (?) magnitude in r band as stored — from photoobj.r | i: PSF/aperture (?) magnitude in i band as stored — from photoobj.i | z: PSF/aperture (?) magnitude in z band as stored — from photoobj.z | ra: right ascension (decimal degrees) — from photoobj.ra | dec: declination (decimal degrees) — from photoobj.dec | b: Galactic latitude (degrees) — from photoobj.b | l: Galactic longitude (degrees) — from photoobj.l | extinction_r: r-band extinction correction (mag) — from photoobj.extinction_r | mjd: Modified Julian Date of observation — from photoobj.mjd | loadversion: data load or pipeline version identifier — from photoobj.loadversion
params.grounded_columns: photoobj.objid | photoobj.run | photoobj.rerun | photoobj.field | photoobj.mode | photoobj.type | photoobj.clean | photoobj.flags | photoobj.rowc | photoobj.colc | photoobj.cmodelmag_u | photoobj.cmodelmag_g | photoobj.cmodelmag_r | photoobj.u | photoobj.g | photoobj.r | photoobj.i | photoobj.z | photoobj.ra | photoobj.dec | photoobj.b | photoobj.l | photoobj.extinction_r | photoobj.mjd | photoobj.loadversion
params.metric: This view exposes no aggregated metrics; all outputs are direct column projections from photoobj (identity mappings). | No derived aggregate expressions are defined in this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to specobj_basic (or specobj_latest_per_bestobj) on objid — safe because photoobj_basic is one-row-per-objid (grain=objid) so attaching one-row-per-object spectral summaries will not duplicate photo measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to photo_type_lookup on type — safe because photo_type_lookup is a normalization/lookup table keyed by type (one row per type); joining will not multiply photoobj_basic rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to specobj_with_photo on objid when that view is one-row-per-specobj linked to objid (verify specobj_with_photo's cardinality) — safe only if that view is constrained to one row per objid; otherwise prefer joining to an aggregated or latest-per-objid spectral view. | unsafe joins (will duplicate rows/measures) — do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views like neighbors_per_obj or photoobj_color_indices without aggregation: neighbors_per_obj and photoobj_color_indices are sibling AGG views (or may represent multiple neighbors/colors) and joining them raw can multiply photoobj_basic rows unless they are pre-aggregated to one row per objid. | unsafe joins — do NOT join to photo_neighbors_join (JOIN) or any neighbor-level table that lists multiple neighbors per objid without first aggregating or restricting to a single neighbor, because that will multiply the one-row-per-objid measures in this view. | If you need counts or summaries from one-to-many siblings (e.g., neighbor counts), join to the aggregated view (neighbors_per_obj) keyed by objid so measures remain one-per-objid. | When composing further aggregates: treat columns from this view as additive attributes per objid (not pre-aggregated sums). If you aggregate after joining to a many-side table, re-aggregate photo measures appropriately (e.g., use AVG/MIN/MAX or GROUP BY photoobj_basic.objid) to avoid accidental duplication. | Planner hint: this view is a projection over photoobj with grain=objid. Any join that maintains a one-to-one or many-to-one relationship from the other side to photoobj_basic (other_side → photoobj_basic) is safe; any join that is one-to-many from photoobj_basic to the other side is unsafe unless the other side is pre-aggregated to one row per objid.

photoobj_basic.description: One-row-per-photometric-object projection with core identifiers, sky coordinates, photometric magnitudes and basic quality flags. Use this to select cohorts of photometric objects or as the base input for joins and aggregations. | Use for: Select photometric objects by position, magnitude or quality flag; Join photometry to spectroscopy or neighbors; Compute distributions/aggregates of magnitudes or colors

Show me the photometrically observed star with the following constraints in its color bands, u - g < 0.4, g - r < 0.7, r - i > 0.4 and i - z > 0.4

photo_type_lookup.name: photo_type_lookup
photo_type_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM photo_type

params.description: Lookup of photo type codes to their human-readable name and description (one row per photo_type.value).
params.when_to_use: Translate or label photo_type.value codes when reporting or filtering photos | Join to photo-level or spectrum-level views to present type name/description | Build dashboards or export data that needs readable photo type labels
params.output_schema: value: integer code representing the photo type (derived from photo_type.value) | name: short human-readable name for the photo type (derived from photo_type.name) | description: longer description of the photo type (derived from photo_type.description)
params.metric: value = photo_type.value | name = photo_type.name | description = photo_type.description
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to photo-level views (e.g., photoobj_basic) on photoobj_basic.type = photo_type.value — safe because photo_type is one-row-per-value (a dimension/lookup), so joining will not duplicate photo-level rows; it only enriches each photo row with type name/description. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to spec-level views that reference a single photo type code per row (e.g., specobj_basic or specobj_with_photo) on their photo_type column = photo_type.value — safe for the same reason as above. | do NOT join photo_type to any one-to-many aggregated view without accounting for multiplicity: for example, joining directly to neighbors_per_obj or photoobj_color_indices (which are AGG/one-to-many summaries keyed to photoobj or field) on a non-matching key would multiply rows if the join is performed across keys that are not the photo type value. Always join on the photo type key (photo_type.value) or first aggregate/reshape the target so that it is one-row-per-photo_type before joining. | do NOT assume photo_type can be joined to photo-level tables on non-type keys (e.g., objid, specobjid, field) — those joins are incorrect and will produce cartesian/duplicated results. | When composing metrics: treat this view as a pure dimension/lookup (no measures to aggregate). If you need counts or other aggregates by photo type, compute them from photoobj_basic (or other fact tables) grouping by photoobj_basic.type, then join that aggregated result to this lookup on type = photo_type.value to safely attach name/description without affecting cardinality.

photo_type_lookup.description: Canonical projection of the photo_type lookup table (one row per type value). Use this to map photoobj.type codes to human-readable names and descriptions when normalizing results. | Use for: Explain type codes associated with photometric objects; Join photometry to type names for reporting or filtering

specobj_basic.name: specobj_basic
specobj_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobjid,
  bestobjid,
  plateid,
  scienceprimary,
  segue2primary,
  survey,
  programname,
  mjd,
  plate,
  fiberid,
  special_target1,
  segue2_target1,
  segue2_target2,
  ancillary_target1,
  ra,
  dec,
  z,
  zerr,
  zwarning,
  class,
  subclass,
  veldisp,
  veldisperr,
  loadversion
FROM specobj

params.description: Provides one-row-per-spectrum (specobj) basic spectroscopic measurements and identifiers for downstream queries and composition.
params.when_to_use: Look up basic spectroscopic properties (redshift, classification, velocity dispersion) for a single spectrum or set of spectra by specobjid, bestobjid, plateid, plate/mjd/fiberid, or sky position. | Filter/select spectroscopic targets by survey/program/primary flags or targeting bits (special_target1, segue2_target1/2, ancillary_target1). | Compose with object-level (photoobj) information or aggregate across spectra when you need a stable per-spectrum input row.
params.output_schema: specobjid: unique identifier for this spectrum (specobj.specobjid) | bestobjid: identifier of the best-matched photometric object for this spectrum (specobj.bestobjid) | plateid: internal plate identifier for the spectroscopic plate (specobj.plateid) | scienceprimary: boolean/int flag indicating this spectrum is marked scienceprimary (specobj.scienceprimary) | segue2primary: boolean/int flag indicating SEGUe2 primary target status (specobj.segue2primary) | survey: survey name or code for this spectrum (specobj.survey) | programname: name of the spectroscopic program that produced this spectrum (specobj.programname) | mjd: Modified Julian Date of the observation (specobj.mjd) | plate: plate number for the observation (specobj.plate) | fiberid: fiber id on the plate for this spectrum (specobj.fiberid) | special_target1: bitmask for special targeting flags (specobj.special_target1) | segue2_target1: SEGUe2 target bitmask field 1 (specobj.segue2_target1) | segue2_target2: SEGUe2 target bitmask field 2 (specobj.segue2_target2) | ancillary_target1: ancillary target bitmask (specobj.ancillary_target1) | ra: right ascension of the spectrum's assigned object (specobj.ra) | dec: declination of the spectrum's assigned object (specobj.dec) | z: redshift measured for this spectrum (specobj.z) | zerr: redshift error (specobj.zerr) | zwarning: zwarning code indicating redshift fitting warnings/issues (specobj.zwarning) | class: spectroscopic classification (e.g., GALAXY, QSO, STAR) (specobj.class) | subclass: subtype string for classification (specobj.subclass) | veldisp: velocity dispersion measurement for the spectrum (specobj.veldisp) | veldisperr: error on velocity dispersion (specobj.veldisperr) | loadversion: pipeline/load version that produced these fields (specobj.loadversion)
params.grounded_columns: specobj.specobjid | specobj.bestobjid | specobj.plateid | specobj.scienceprimary | specobj.segue2primary | specobj.survey | specobj.programname | specobj.mjd | specobj.plate | specobj.fiberid | specobj.special_target1 | specobj.segue2_target1 | specobj.segue2_target2 | specobj.ancillary_target1 | specobj.ra | specobj.dec | specobj.z | specobj.zerr | specobj.zwarning | specobj.class | specobj.subclass | specobj.veldisp | specobj.veldisperr | specobj.loadversion
params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics are defined in this view; all outputs are direct column projections from specobj. | If you need counts or aggregated statistics (e.g., COUNT(specobjid), AVG(z), STDDEV(veldisp)), compute them by aggregating over specobj_basic rows.
params.composition: Safe joins (one-to-one or many-to-one that will NOT duplicate rows/measures): |  - Join to specobj_latest_per_bestobj on specobj_basic.bestobjid = specobj_latest_per_bestobj.bestobjid — safe because specobj_latest_per_bestobj is one-row-per-bestobj (it picks a latest spec) so joining will at most match one latest-spectrum row per bestobjid; however be explicit about which specobj you'd prefer when combining spectrum-level fields. |  - Join to photoobj_basic on specobj_basic.bestobjid = photoobj_basic.bestobjid (or photoobj_basic.objid = specobj_basic.bestobjid if that is the key in photoobj_basic) — safe because photoobj_basic is one-row-per-photometric-object, so it will not multiply spectroscopic rows. |  - Join to photo_type_lookup on photoobj_basic.type (or other photometric dimension tables keyed one-to-one on objid/type) — safe when joining on a key with at most one match per left row. |  - Join to NORM tables like galspecline_exists when they are one-row-per-specobj or one-row-per-bestobj and you join on the same key — safe if the normalization guarantees one row per key. |  | Unsafe joins (will multiply rows/measures unless you re-aggregate or deduplicate first): |  - Do NOT directly join to photo_neighbors_join, photoobj_color_indices, neighbors_per_obj, photoobj_running_counts_by_field, or any AGG/WIN sibling that is one-to-many per specobj/bestobj without careful aggregation. Those sibling views produce multiple rows per object/field and will duplicate specobj_basic rows and any derived counts if joined directly. |  - Do NOT join to specobj (the base table) or any raw-spectrum-level table that has multiple rows per specobjid/observation unless you filter to a unique key first; specobj_basic is one-row-per-specobjid, but joining to tables with multiple rows per specobjid multiplies rows. |  | Guidance for safe composition patterns: |  - If you must combine with a one-to-many view (e.g., neighbors_per_obj which lists neighbors), first aggregate that view to one row per key (e.g., COUNT(neighbor_id) AS neighbor_count GROUP BY key) and then join to specobj_basic on the key. That preserves correct per-spectrum measures. |  - When joining by bestobjid to object-level data, ensure the object-level view is one-row-per-bestobj (photoobj_basic) or aggregate it to one row per bestobj before joining. |  - When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., number of spectra per bestobj), aggregate specobj_basic (GROUP BY bestobjid) rather than joining specobj_basic to a one-to-many table expecting to preserve uniqueness. |  | Examples of safe join keys: |  - specobj_basic.specobjid = <other_view>.specobjid — safe only if other_view is one-row-per-specobjid. |  - specobj_basic.bestobjid = photoobj_basic.bestobjid (or objid) — safe because photoobj_basic is one-row-per-object. |  | Documenting multiplicity reasoning: |  - specobj_basic has grain = one row per specobjid (spectrum). Any join to another relation that is guaranteed to be at-most-one row per specobjid or per bestobjid preserves this grain. Joins to relations that are one-to-many relative to specobjid or bestobjid will multiply the number of resulting rows and thus duplicate any measures that would be aggregated without compensating aggregations or DISTINCT counts.

specobj_basic.description: One-row-per-spectroscopic-object projection with identifiers, linking to photometric object via bestobjid, sky coordinates, redshift and classification fields. Use as the canonical spectroscopic row for joins and filtering. | Use for: Link spectroscopy to photometry via bestobjid; Select spectroscopic targets by redshift, class or quality flags; Aggregate spectroscopic measures by program or plate

Find Galaxy that are photometrically observable
Show me object id, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observed galaxy in a certain area, of which the right ascension is between 185 and 186, declination is bertween 15 and 16.
Find properties of all spectroscopic observed galaxy,  whose right ascension is greater than 185 and less than 186, declination is greater than 15 and less than 16.
Fetch me the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy with the color band magnitude g brighter than 18.0 but fainter than 17 and redshift lower than 0.05

specobj_with_photo.name: specobj_with_photo
specobj_with_photo.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.plateid,
  s.scienceprimary,
  s.survey,
  s.programname,
  s.mjd AS mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid,
  s.ra AS ra,
  s.dec AS dec,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.zwarning,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode AS mode,
  p.type AS type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z AS z_mag,
  p.extinction_r
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid

params.description: Provides one-row-per-spectrum (specobjid) spectral records augmented with the matched photometric object attributes from photoobj (joined by bestobjid = objid).
params.when_to_use: Find spectra with their matched photometry (e.g., get coordinates, magnitudes, extinction and spectral redshift/zerr for a given specobjid or bestobjid). | Filter or aggregate spectra by photometric properties (colors, magnitudes) after composing with color/index views or aggregations. | Join spectral-level analyses (z, class, scienceprimary) to photometric-level datasets when you need exactly one spectral row per spectrum.
params.output_schema: specobjid: unique identifier of the spectral extraction (derived from specobj.specobjid) | bestobjid: identifier of the matched best photometric object (derived from specobj.bestobjid) | plateid: spectroscopic plate identifier (derived from specobj.plateid) | scienceprimary: boolean/int flag indicating whether this spectrum is the primary science spectrum for the object (derived from specobj.scienceprimary) | survey: survey name/source for the spectrum (derived from specobj.survey) | programname: targeting/program label for the spectrum (derived from specobj.programname) | mjd: Modified Julian Date of the spectroscopic observation (derived from specobj.mjd) | plate: plate number for the spectroscopic observation (derived from specobj.plate) | fiberid: fiber identifier on the plate for the spectrum (derived from specobj.fiberid) | ra: right ascension (J2000) of the spectrum/object (derived from specobj.ra) | dec: declination (J2000) of the spectrum/object (derived from specobj.dec) | z: spectroscopic redshift (derived from specobj.z) | zerr: uncertainty on the spectroscopic redshift (derived from specobj.zerr) | zwarning: z pipeline warning flags (derived from specobj.zwarning) | class: spectral classification (STAR/GALAXY/QSO, derived from specobj.class) | subclass: spectral subclass (derived from specobj.subclass) | objid: photometric object id matched to the spectrum (derived from photoobj.objid via the LEFT JOIN on bestobjid = objid) | run: photometric run id (derived from photoobj.run) | rerun: photometric rerun processing id (derived from photoobj.rerun) | field: photometric field id (derived from photoobj.field) | mode: photometric mode (derived from photoobj.mode) | type: photometric object type (derived from photoobj.type) | clean: photometric 'clean' flag (derived from photoobj.clean) | flags: photometric flags bitmask (derived from photoobj.flags) | u: u-band PSF/aperture magnitude as provided in photoobj.u | g: g-band magnitude from photoobj.g | r: r-band magnitude from photoobj.r | i: i-band magnitude from photoobj.i | z_mag: z-band magnitude from photoobj.z (aliased to avoid collision with specobj.z) | extinction_r: r-band extinction correction from photoobj.extinction_r
params.grounded_columns: specobj.specobjid | specobj.bestobjid | specobj.plateid | specobj.scienceprimary | specobj.survey | specobj.programname | specobj.mjd | specobj.plate | specobj.fiberid | specobj.ra | specobj.dec | specobj.z | specobj.zerr | specobj.zwarning | specobj.class | specobj.subclass | photoobj.objid | photoobj.run | photoobj.rerun | photoobj.field | photoobj.mode | photoobj.type | photoobj.clean | photoobj.flags | photoobj.u | photoobj.g | photoobj.r | photoobj.i | photoobj.z | photoobj.extinction_r
params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics are computed in this view; all outputs are direct column projections or simple aliases. | If used as a metric source, treat the view as providing point-measures at the specobjid grain (e.g., count(specobjid) is the number of spectral rows).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dim/specobj_basic on specobjid — safe because specobj_basic is one-row-per-specobjid (same grain) so measures from specobj_with_photo will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to specobj_latest_per_bestobj on specobjid or bestobjid only if that view is one-row-per-specobjid or one-row-per-bestobj as documented — safe when keys match the view's grain (specobjid) and the other view guarantees uniqueness on that key. | DO NOT join directly to photoobj_basic or other photoobj one-to-many views without ensuring uniqueness on photoobj.objid: this view already LEFT JOINs photoobj by bestobjid=objid producing at most one matched photoobj row per specobj (assuming photoobj.objid is unique). If you join again to photoobj-derived views that expand photoobj into multiple rows (for example, photo_neighbors_join or any AGG producing multiple rows per objid if not aggregated), you will multiply spec-level measures. | Do NOT join to neighbors_per_obj, photoobj_running_counts_by_field, photoobj_color_indices, photo_neighbors_join, or other one-to-many neighbor/measurement expansions on objid without aggregating those expansions to one row per objid (or per specobjid) first — otherwise counts or summed measures computed at the specobjid grain will be duplicated. | Safe composition pattern: to augment with photometric aggregates, first aggregate the one-to-many photo-level table to one row per objid (e.g., compute color indices or counts) and then join that aggregated result to specobj_with_photo on bestobjid = objid. That preserves one-row-per-specobjid and keeps measures unduplicated. | If you need to join to a table keyed by bestobjid (one row per bestobjid), join on specobj_with_photo.bestobjid = other.bestobjid — safe because bestobjid per specobj is one value and the other side is one-row-per-bestobjid. | When building higher-level metrics (e.g., number of spectra per field), perform the aggregation after joining any one-to-many enrichments, or pre-aggregate the enrichment side to ensure cardinality remains 1:1 with this view's grain (specobjid).

specobj_with_photo.description: Denormalized join of specobj to its matched photometric best object (photoobj) including spectroscopic redshift and photometric magnitudes. Use this when combining spectroscopic properties with photometry for the same object. | Use for: Compare photometry and spectroscopy for the same targets; Filter spectroscopic samples by photometric colors or quality; Compute color vs redshift trends

Fetch me the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy with the color band magnitude g brighter than 18.0 but fainter than 17 and redshift lower than 0.05

neighbors_per_obj.name: neighbors_per_obj
neighbors_per_obj.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  COUNT(neighborobjid) AS neighbor_count,
  MIN(distance) AS min_distance,
  AVG(distance) AS avg_distance
FROM neighbors
GROUP BY objid

params.description: Per-object summary of how many neighbors each object has and the distance statistics (min and average) to those neighbors.
params.when_to_use: Find the number of neighboring objects for a given objid | Rank or filter objects by how close their nearest neighbor is (min_distance) | Compute average neighbor distance per object for quality or clustering analyses | Join as an object-level enrichment when building object-level reports (one row per objid)
params.output_schema: objid: unique identifier for the primary object; sourced from neighbors.objid (grouping key) | neighbor_count: integer count of neighborobjid values for that objid; derived from COUNT(neighborobjid) over neighbors | min_distance: minimum observed distance between objid and its neighbors; derived from MIN(distance) over neighbors | avg_distance: average distance between objid and its neighbors; derived from AVG(distance) over neighbors
params.metric: neighbor_count = COUNT(neighborobjid)  -- count of neighbor rows per neighbors.objid | min_distance = MIN(distance)           -- minimum distance value per neighbors.objid | avg_distance = AVG(distance)           -- arithmetic mean of distance per neighbors.objid
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to object/dimension-level tables or views that are one-row-per-objid (for example: photoobj_basic, specobj_basic, specobj_with_photo, specobj_latest_per_bestobj) ON neighbors_per_obj.objid = <other>.objid — safe because neighbors_per_obj is exactly one row per objid (grouped), so its aggregated measures are not duplicated. | Safe to join to lookup or normalization tables (e.g., photo_type_lookup, galspecline_exists) on objid or related object keys when those tables are one-row-per-objid or are pure lookups, because they don't multiply rows. | Do NOT join directly to any table or view that has multiple rows per objid (one-to-many) such as a raw neighbors table, repeated measurements, or any detailed-event table, without re-aggregating the detail first — doing so will multiply neighbor_count, min_distance and avg_distance and thus corrupt the measures. | If you need to combine neighbors_per_obj with a one-to-many detail (e.g., to compute weighted averages or join per-neighbor records), either: (a) aggregate that detail to one row per objid before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate to the desired grain (objid) so that measures are recomputed correctly. | When composing further aggregates (for example, computing average neighbor_count across a subset of objects), treat neighbor_count as a measured value to be aggregated (e.g., SUM(neighbor_count)/COUNT(objid) or AVG(neighbor_count)) — avoid summing pre-aggregated averages (avg_distance) without using appropriate weighting if you intend a global average distance across neighbors.

neighbors_per_obj.description: Aggregated neighbor statistics per objid: total neighbor count, minimum distance to any neighbor, and average neighbor distance. Use to quantify local crowding or nearest-neighbor distance distributions. | Use for: Find isolated objects (large min_distance or zero neighbors); Rank objects by neighbor density; Join neighbor density to photometry or spectroscopy

photoobj_color_indices.name: photoobj_color_indices
photoobj_color_indices.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  u,
  g,
  r,
  i,
  z,
  (u - g) AS u_minus_g,
  (g - r) AS g_minus_r,
  (r - i) AS r_minus_i,
  (i - z) AS i_minus_z,
  (cmodelmag_u - cmodelmag_r) AS cmodel_u_minus_r
FROM photoobj

params.description: Provides per-object photometric magnitudes and color indices (differences) computed from the photoobj table, at the grain of one row per objid.
params.when_to_use: Get the broadband magnitudes (u,g,r,i,z) for a specific objid or set of objids | Compute or filter by simple colors (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) for objects | Join per-object magnitudes/colors into catalogs (e.g., to combine with spectroscopy or neighbors) when you need one-row-per-obj photometry | Use as a building block in downstream aggregations (e.g., field- or sample-level color distributions) or derived metrics (e.g., color cuts) without re-deriving base magnitudes
params.output_schema: objid: unique object identifier — directly from photoobj.objid | u: u-band magnitude — directly from photoobj.u | g: g-band magnitude — directly from photoobj.g | r: r-band magnitude — directly from photoobj.r | i: i-band magnitude — directly from photoobj.i | z: z-band magnitude — directly from photoobj.z | u_minus_g: u - g color (u minus g) — computed as (photoobj.u - photoobj.g) | g_minus_r: g - r color (g minus r) — computed as (photoobj.g - photoobj.r) | r_minus_i: r - i color (r minus i) — computed as (photoobj.r - photoobj.i) | i_minus_z: i - z color (i minus z) — computed as (photoobj.i - photoobj.z) | cmodel_u_minus_r: cmodelmag_u - cmodelmag_r color using cmodel magnitudes — computed as (photoobj.cmodelmag_u - photoobj.cmodelmag_r)
params.grounded_columns: photoobj.objid | photoobj.u | photoobj.g | photoobj.r | photoobj.i | photoobj.z | photoobj.cmodelmag_u | photoobj.cmodelmag_r
params.metric: u_minus_g = photoobj.u - photoobj.g | g_minus_r = photoobj.g - photoobj.r | r_minus_i = photoobj.r - photoobj.i | i_minus_z = photoobj.i - photoobj.z | cmodel_u_minus_r = photoobj.cmodelmag_u - photoobj.cmodelmag_r
params.composition: Join to photoobj_basic on photoobj_basic.objid = photoobj_color_indices.objid — safe because both views are one-row-per-objid (no duplication of rows or measures). | Join to specobj_with_photo or specobj_basic on specobj.objid = photoobj_color_indices.objid — safe when specobj rows are one-per-objid (check specobj view grain); if specobj is one-to-many per objid (e.g., multiple spectra), aggregate or restrict specobj to one row per objid (e.g., latest) before joining to avoid duplicating photo measures. | Join to specobj_latest_per_bestobj on objid = photoobj_color_indices.objid — safe because specobj_latest_per_bestobj is a ranked view that provides at most one row per bestobj/objid, preventing duplication. | Join to photoobj_running_counts_by_field or neighbors_per_obj only if those views are one-row-per-objid (verify their grain). If they are aggregated to one-row-per-objid (like neighbors_per_obj declared AGG with grain ['objid']) it is safe; if they are one-to-many, you must aggregate them first. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., per-detection tables, multiple neighbors without aggregation, or raw spectra if multiple per objid) without re-aggregating the many-side, because that will multiply rows and therefore duplicate/scale the magnitudes and color measures incorrectly. | If you need population-level aggregates (counts, averages of colors) after joining to a many-side, perform the join using a pre-aggregated many-side (e.g., neighbors_per_obj aggregated per objid) or re-aggregate after the join with explicit aggregation functions and GROUP BY photoobj_color_indices.objid to preserve correctness. | When composing with JOIN views in this DB: photo_neighbors_join and photoobj_with_photo are JOIN types — verify their resultant grain before joining; prefer joining to normalized/lookups (photo_type_lookup) or ranked/aggregated views (specobj_latest_per_bestobj, neighbors_per_obj) that guarantee one-row-per-objid for cardinality-safe composition.

photoobj_color_indices.description: Per-object derived photometric color indices and a simple magnitude summary. Useful for color-based selection or for feeding into ranking/aggregation pipelines. | Use for: Color selection (e.g., select objects in color boxes); Compute color distributions or color-color diagrams; Combine colors with spectroscopy for population studies

photo_neighbors_join.name: photo_neighbors_join
photo_neighbors_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode,
  p1.ra AS ra,
  p1.dec AS dec,
  p1.u AS u,
  p1.g AS g,
  p1.r AS r,
  p1.i AS i,
  p1.z AS z,
  p2.ra AS neighbor_ra,
  p2.dec AS neighbor_dec,
  p2.u AS neighbor_u,
  p2.g AS neighbor_g,
  p2.r AS neighbor_r,
  p2.i AS neighbor_i,
  p2.z AS neighbor_z
FROM neighbors n
LEFT JOIN photoobj p1
  ON n.objid = p1.objid
LEFT JOIN photoobj p2
  ON n.neighborobjid = p2.objid

params.description: Pairs of photo objects and their neighboring photo objects with positional, photometric, and neighbor metadata (one row per neighbor relationship).
params.when_to_use: Get all neighbors (within whatever radius is encoded in neighbors) for a set of objects, with both objects' RA/Dec and ugriz magnitudes. | Filter neighbor pairs by distance, object type, mode, or photometry and then aggregate (e.g., count neighbors within a distance bin). | Compose into spatial or photometric joins where you need direct access to both the primary object and neighbor attributes in the same row. | Build higher-level aggregations per object (e.g., nearest neighbor magnitude, neighbor counts by type) by aggregating this view rather than re-joining base tables.
params.output_schema: objid: primary object identifier — derived from neighbors.objid | neighborobjid: neighbor object identifier — derived from neighbors.neighborobjid | distance: separation/distance between objid and neighborobjid — derived from neighbors.distance | type: type code for the primary object — derived from neighbors.type | neighbortype: type code for the neighbor object — derived from neighbors.neighbortype | mode: mode flag for the primary object — derived from neighbors.mode | neighbormode: mode flag for the neighbor object — derived from neighbors.neighbormode | ra: right ascension (degrees) of the primary object — derived from photoobj.ra (aliased p1.ra) | dec: declination (degrees) of the primary object — derived from photoobj.dec (aliased p1.dec) | u: u-band magnitude of the primary object — derived from photoobj.u (aliased p1.u) | g: g-band magnitude of the primary object — derived from photoobj.g (aliased p1.g) | r: r-band magnitude of the primary object — derived from photoobj.r (aliased p1.r) | i: i-band magnitude of the primary object — derived from photoobj.i (aliased p1.i) | z: z-band magnitude of the primary object — derived from photoobj.z (aliased p1.z) | neighbor_ra: right ascension (degrees) of the neighbor object — derived from photoobj.ra (aliased p2.ra) | neighbor_dec: declination (degrees) of the neighbor object — derived from photoobj.dec (aliased p2.dec) | neighbor_u: u-band magnitude of the neighbor object — derived from photoobj.u (aliased p2.u) | neighbor_g: g-band magnitude of the neighbor object — derived from photoobj.g (aliased p2.g) | neighbor_r: r-band magnitude of the neighbor object — derived from photoobj.r (aliased p2.r) | neighbor_i: i-band magnitude of the neighbor object — derived from photoobj.i (aliased p2.i) | neighbor_z: z-band magnitude of the neighbor object — derived from photoobj.z (aliased p2.z)
params.grounded_columns: neighbors.objid | neighbors.neighborobjid | neighbors.distance | neighbors.type | neighbors.neighbortype | neighbors.mode | neighbors.neighbormode | photoobj.objid AS p1.objid (used via ON n.objid = p1.objid) | photoobj.ra AS p1.ra | photoobj.dec AS p1.dec | photoobj.u AS p1.u | photoobj.g AS p1.g | photoobj.r AS p1.r | photoobj.i AS p1.i | photoobj.z AS p1.z | photoobj.objid AS p2.objid (used via ON n.neighborobjid = p2.objid) | photoobj.ra AS p2.ra | photoobj.dec AS p2.dec | photoobj.u AS p2.u | photoobj.g AS p2.g | photoobj.r AS p2.r | photoobj.i AS p2.i | photoobj.z AS p2.z
params.metric: objid = neighbors.objid | neighborobjid = neighbors.neighborobjid | distance = neighbors.distance | type = neighbors.type | neighbortype = neighbors.neighbortype | mode = neighbors.mode | neighbormode = neighbors.neighbormode | ra = p1.ra | dec = p1.dec | u = p1.u | g = p1.g | r = p1.r | i = p1.i | z = p1.z | neighbor_ra = p2.ra | neighbor_dec = p2.dec | neighbor_u = p2.u | neighbor_g = p2.g | neighbor_r = p2.r | neighbor_i = p2.i | neighbor_z = p2.z
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a dimension that is one-row-per-objid (for example a photoobj or photoobj_basic view keyed by objid) on objid or neighborobjid — safe because this view already contains one row per (objid, neighborobjid) pair from neighbors, and joining to another one-to-one-per-objid source will not duplicate neighbor rows. | cardinality-SAFE: aggregate this view by objid first before joining to an object-level summary (for example to compute neighbor counts, nearest neighbor distance, or mean neighbor magnitude) — safe because aggregation reduces the (objid, neighborobjid) multiplicity to one row per objid. | DO NOT join this view directly to any table/view that is one-to-many from objid (for example a spectral-lines table or any observations table with multiple rows per objid) without first aggregating or deduplicating the many-side. Doing so will multiply the neighbor rows and therefore duplicate counts/measures derived from this view. | DO NOT join this view to another neighbors-like table keyed by the same (objid, neighborobjid) pair in a way that produces multiple matching rows per pair unless you intend row-multiplication. If you must combine, join on the exact pair keys (objid, neighborobjid) and ensure the other table is one-row-per-pair. | When composing into larger queries, preserve the (objid, neighborobjid) uniqueness from neighbors as the safe atomic unit. If you need per-object metrics, compute aggregates (COUNT, MIN(distance), AVG(neighbor_r), etc.) grouped by objid from this view and then join aggregated results back to other per-object dimensions. | Examples of safe joins: |  - JOIN photoobj_basic PB ON photo_neighbors_join.objid = PB.objid  — safe because photoobj_basic is one-row-per-objid. |  - JOIN photoobj_basic PB2 ON photo_neighbors_join.neighborobjid = PB2.objid  — safe for the neighbor side. | Examples of unsafe joins (will duplicate rows/measures unless you pre-aggregate): |  - JOIN specobj_with_photo S ON photo_neighbors_join.objid = S.objid  — unsafe if specobj_with_photo can have multiple spectra per photoobj (one-to-many). |  - JOIN galspecline_exists G ON photo_neighbors_join.objid = G.objid  — unsafe if G is one-to-many; instead aggregate G to one row per objid (e.g., EXISTS boolean) before joining.

photo_neighbors_join.description: Explode neighbor edges by joining neighbors to the photometric attributes of both endpoints. Each row is one neighbor relationship with photometry for objid and neighborobjid. Useful when analyzing pair properties or computing pairwise differences. | Use for: Compute photometric differences between neighboring objects; Filter neighbor pairs by type or distance; Aggregate pair statistics (e.g., average magnitude difference vs distance)
validated_on: Show me the object id, right ascension and declination of photometrically observed Galaxy, of which the the right ascension in a range of from 140.9 to 141.1, the magnitude g is less than 18.0 and the difference of magnitude u and g is higher than 2.2
counter_examples: Show me the photometrically observed star with the following constraints in its color bands, u - g < 0.4, g - r < 0.7, r - i > 0.4 and i - z > 0.4

specobj_latest_per_bestobj.name: specobj_latest_per_bestobj
specobj_latest_per_bestobj.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobjid,
  bestobjid,
  plateid,
  scienceprimary,
  mjd,
  loadversion,
  z,
  zerr,
  zwarning,
  class,
  subclass,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bestobjid ORDER BY COALESCE(mjd, -1) DESC, COALESCE(loadversion, -1) DESC, specobjid) AS spec_rank
FROM specobj

params.description: For each unique astronomical object ('bestobjid'), return the single most-recent (by observation date and loadversion) spectral record and its spec-level identifiers and redshift information.
params.when_to_use: Get the latest spectrum information per bestobjid (one row per object) to annotate catalogs with the most recent spec record. | Compose higher-level queries that need one canonical spectrum per object (e.g., match to photometry, compute object-level redshift summaries, or join to object metadata) without double-counting multiple spectra. | Filter or rank objects by their latest spectrum properties such as z, zerr, zwarning, class, or mjd.
params.output_schema: specobjid: unique identifier of the spectral record chosen as the 'latest' per bestobjid; sourced from specobj.specobjid | bestobjid: the canonical object id that groups multiple spectra for the same astrophysical object; sourced from specobj.bestobjid | plateid: spectroscopic plate identifier for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.plateid | scienceprimary: science primary flag of the chosen spec record (usually 1 if primary); sourced from specobj.scienceprimary | mjd: modified Julian date of the observation for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.mjd | loadversion: pipeline load/version indicator for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.loadversion | z: redshift measured for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.z | zerr: redshift uncertainty for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.zerr | zwarning: redshift warning flag(s) for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.zwarning | class: spectroscopic classification (e.g., STAR, GALAXY, QSO) for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.class | subclass: spectroscopic subclass for the chosen spec record; sourced from specobj.subclass | spec_rank: integer rank assigned by ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by bestobjid ordering COALESCE(mjd, -1) DESC, COALESCE(loadversion, -1) DESC, specobjid; 1 indicates the chosen 'latest' record
params.grounded_columns: specobj.specobjid | specobj.bestobjid | specobj.plateid | specobj.scienceprimary | specobj.mjd | specobj.loadversion | specobj.z | specobj.zerr | specobj.zwarning | specobj.class | specobj.subclass
params.metric: spec_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY specobj.bestobjid ORDER BY COALESCE(specobj.mjd, -1) DESC, COALESCE(specobj.loadversion, -1) DESC, specobj.specobjid) | latest_row_per_bestobj (implicit selection) = choose rows where spec_rank = 1 (this view exposes spec_rank to allow consumers to filter to spec_rank = 1 for the canonical latest row)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to dimensional/one-row-per-object views (example: specobj_basic) on bestobjid — safe because specobj_latest_per_bestobj is one-row-per-bestobjid when consumers restrict to spec_rank = 1, so measures (z, zerr) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE: join to photoobj_basic or other one-row-per-bestobjid photometry views on bestobjid — safe when those photo views are themselves one-row-per-bestobjid (no multiplication of rows). | cardinality-SAFE: join to photo_type_lookup or other lookup/norm tables on type/code columns — safe because lookups are 1-to-1 for the code. | NOT safe to directly join to one-to-many tables or views without re-aggregation: do NOT join this view (unless you first filter to spec_rank = 1) to tables that contain multiple rows per bestobjid (for example: neighbors_per_obj, photo_neighbors_join, galspecline_exists if they are multi-row) because that will multiply the spec rows and effectively duplicate measures such as z and specobjid. | If joining to a one-to-many table is necessary, either: (a) pre-aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per bestobjid (e.g., COUNT, MAX) before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate the combined result to the desired grain (bestobjid) to avoid overcounting. | When composing further WINDOW functions or ROW_NUMBER() on this view, ensure you restrict to spec_rank = 1 if you require a single canonical spec per bestobjid, because the underlying SQL produces multiple specobj rows per bestobjid prior to that filter. | This view exposes spec_rank so downstream planners can safely select WHERE spec_rank = 1 to obtain exactly one row per bestobjid; any join guidance above assumes that restriction when claiming one-row-per-bestobjid behavior.

specobj_latest_per_bestobj.description: For each bestobjid (photometric object), rank associated spectroscopic records by mjd and loadversion to produce a deterministic latest-per-bestobj view. Exposes a rank so callers can select top-N per bestobjid. | Use for: Select the most recent spectrum for each photometric object; Resolve duplicate spectroscopic records per photometric match; Create top-N spectroscopic samples per object

photoobj_running_counts_by_field.name: photoobj_running_counts_by_field
photoobj_running_counts_by_field.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  run,
  field,
  objid AS ordering_objid,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY field ORDER BY objid ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_count_in_field
FROM photoobj

params.description: For each photo object (objid) this view gives its run and field and the cumulative count of photo objects within the same field ordered by objid (a running count per field).
params.when_to_use: Ask for the position/rank of an individual photo object within its field (e.g., 'what is the running index of objid X within its field?'). | Compute field-level cumulative distributions or percentiles when combined with field totals (e.g., to compute fraction of objects up to a given objid). | Compose with other per-object lookups to add a stable monotonic ordering / per-field sequence number for each photo object. | Build pagination or windowed slices inside a field when you need a deterministically ordered index per field.
params.output_schema: objid: unique identifier of the photo object — directly from photoobj.objid | run: survey/run identifier for the photo object — directly from photoobj.run | field: field identifier in which the photo object was observed — directly from photoobj.field | ordering_objid: same as objid; provided to make the ordering column explicit for composed queries — derived as objid (photoobj.objid) | running_count_in_field: running count (1..N) of objects in the same field ordered by objid, i.e. the cumulative number of rows up to and including this objid within that field — defined by COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY field ORDER BY objid ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) on photoobj rows
params.metric: running_count_in_field = COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY photoobj.field ORDER BY photoobj.objid ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dim-like or one-row-per-objid views on objid (for example photoobj_basic) — safe because this view is one-row-per-objid (grain = ['objid']) so joining on objid does not duplicate running_count_in_field. | safe: join to photoobj_basic (SEL) on photoobj_basic.objid = photoobj_running_counts_by_field.objid — one-to-one by objid, measures preserved. | safe: join to photoobj_color_indices (AGG) only if that view is also one-row-per-objid; verify its grain before join. If it is one-row-per-objid, join on objid is safe. | unsafe without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to any sibling that is one-to-many per objid (for example neighbors_per_obj (AGG) or photo_neighbors_join (JOIN) if they produce multiple rows per objid) on objid without first aggregating the many-side back to one row per objid — otherwise running_count_in_field will be duplicated/multiplied. | unsafe without re-aggregation: do NOT join to views with grain = field (many objids per field) expecting to preserve running_count_in_field as an atomic measure; joining field->many-rows will multiply rows unless you join on objid or you re-aggregate after the join. | If you need field-level totals together with this running count, compute field_total = COUNT(*) FROM photoobj GROUP BY field (or use an existing field-aggregated view) and then join on field — safe when field_total is one-row-per-field because joining one-row-per-field to one-row-per-objid on field is one-to-many but does not duplicate the per-objid running_count (it attaches the field_total as an attribute). | When composing further windowing or aggregation: to aggregate running_count_in_field (for example sum or avg across a set of objids), perform the aggregation in the outer query; do not assume distributive properties — running_count_in_field is a positional metric, not a simple additive measure across partitions.

photoobj_running_counts_by_field.description: Per-photoobj running count within each field ordered by objid. Exposes a running_total so callers can compute densities or percentile positions within a field. | Use for: Compute per-field cumulative distributions or percentiles; Identify objects by rank order within a field

galspecline_exists.name: galspecline_exists
galspecline_exists.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobjid,
  1 AS has_galspecline
FROM galspecline

params.description: For each spectrum object (specobjid) that has at least one row in the galspecline table, emit a single row marking presence with has_galspecline = 1.
params.when_to_use: Determine whether a given specobjid has any associated galspecline rows (exists-check). | Filter or join analyses to include only specobjids that have (or do not have) emission/absorption line records present in galspecline. | Compose higher-level aggregations or counts of specobjid-level presence of galspecline (e.g., join to specobj_basic and then aggregate by class). | Build indicators/features for models that require a binary flag for whether line measurements exist for a spectrum.
params.output_schema: specobjid: unique identifier of the spectrum object (derived directly from galspecline.specobjid). | has_galspecline: integer flag = 1 indicating that at least one galspecline row exists for the specobjid (derived as literal 1 in the view for each returned specobjid).
params.metric: has_galspecline = 1 (literal flag applied per output row).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or one-row-per-specobjid views/tables (for example, join to specobj_basic on specobjid) — safe because galspecline_exists has at most one row per specobjid (the view's declared grain is specobjid), so joining on specobjid will not duplicate this view's indicator. | Safe to join to specobj_with_photo, specobj_latest_per_bestobj, or any other view that is one-row-per-specobjid on specobjid for enrichment without re-aggregation. | Do NOT join directly (inner/left) to one-to-many tables or views keyed by specobjid that have multiple rows per specobjid (for example, the underlying galspecline table itself, or any AGG/WIN/JOIN views that produce multiple rows per specobjid) without first aggregating those tables to one row per specobjid. Doing so will multiply rows and thus multiply the meaning of has_galspecline unless you aggregate (e.g., MAX(has_galspecline) or ANY_VALUE) back to one row per specobjid. | If composing metrics across joins where the downstream need is an aggregated metric (counts, sums, averages) per specobjid, prefer joining this view and then using aggregation functions (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT specobjid) filtered by has_galspecline = 1, or MAX(has_galspecline) when combining with many-to-one joins) so the binary indicator is not duplicated. | When joining to tables keyed by a different grain (for example, photoobj tables keyed by objid or observations keyed by visit/field), join via a one-row-per-specobjid bridge (such as specobj_basic or specobj_with_photo) or aggregate the other side to specobjid first to preserve cardinality.

galspecline_exists.description: Simple presence flag for specobjid indicating whether a galspecline row exists. Useful to join to specobj to quickly filter or label spectra that have associated galspecline products. | Use for: Flag spectra that have additional derived products; Join to specobj to restrict to spectra with galspecline

photoobj_star_types.name: photoobj_star_types
photoobj_star_types.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.value AS photo_type_value,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name,
  pt.description AS photo_type_description
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  photo_type AS pt
    ON pt.value = p.type
WHERE
  (
    LOWER(COALESCE(pt.name, '')) LIKE '%star%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(pt.description, '')) LIKE '%star%'
  )
photoobj_star_types.description: Map photoobj rows to photo_type entries that indicate stellar classifications (photo_type rows whose name or description mention 'star'), producing a denormalized relation of photoobj with the matching photo_type.value and metadata.

photo_with_spectra.name: photo_with_spectra
photo_with_spectra.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra   AS ra,
  p.dec  AS dec,
  -- matched_specobjid: choose the linked specobj.specobjid when available;
  -- match if specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid OR specobj.specobjid = photoobj.objid
  -- lift literal '1' as a placeholder for any priority value (no literals specific to question otherwise)
  COALESCE(s.specobjid, s_bybest.specobjid) AS matched_specobjid
FROM
  photoobj AS p
  -- join on specobj where specobj.specobjid equals the photo's objid (direct specobjid match)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT sb.specobjid
    FROM specobj AS sb
    WHERE sb.specobjid = p.objid
    LIMIT 1
  ) s ON true
  -- also consider specobj rows where bestobjid matches the photo's objid
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT sb2.specobjid
    FROM specobj AS sb2
    WHERE sb2.bestobjid = p.objid
    LIMIT 1
  ) s_bybest ON s.specobjid IS NULL AND s_bybest.specobjid IS NOT NULL
WHERE
  -- require that at least one matching specobj exists (either direct or via bestobjid)
  (s.specobjid IS NOT NULL OR s_bybest.specobjid IS NOT NULL)
photo_with_spectra.description: Denormalized view joining photometric objects to available spectra. One row per photoobj.objid that has at least one matching specobj (by bestobjid or specobjid). Exposes photo coordinates and the linked specobjid for existence checks.

  p.objid,
  -- lift literals: none needed for this simple arithmetic
  -- carry canonical mags through; use cmodel mags when available else fallback to psf/model? schema provides cmodelmag_* in photoobj_basic,
  -- but this view should use canonical photometry available in photoobj (u,g,r,i,z). We'll compute color differences directly.
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM
  photoobj AS p
photoobj_colors_derived.description: Per-photoobj derived color columns (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) computed from canonical photometry; one row per photoobj.objid. Does not apply semantic filters (e.g. type) so it can be reused for star/galaxy cohorts.

photoobj_star_candidates.name: photoobj_star_candidates
photoobj_star_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type
FROM
  -- base photoobj table; using photoobj_basic view when available keeps this view composable.
  -- Lift the star type code out as a literal to make the view reusable.
  photoobj_basic p
WHERE
  -- require the object's type equals the 'star' type code (lifted literal)
  p.type = 6
  -- require magnitude columns present (no additional magnitude thresholds)
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_candidates.description: Row-level cohort of photometric objects that are classified as stars (photoobj.type = star type code). Does not apply magnitude thresholds beyond requiring magnitude columns to be non-null. Useful as a base cohort for magnitude/color selections.

photoobj_basic_photometry.name: photoobj_basic_photometry
photoobj_basic_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- canonical/raw photometry columns (lifted directly; literals avoided)
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.extinction_r,
  -- explicit names for ambiguous flag/clean columns (preserve original types)
  p.flags,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj AS p

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic magnitude or type filters; only projects and renames columns

photoobj_basic_photometry.description: Normalized projection of photoobj with canonical photometry columns (u,g,r,i,z), positions, and basic flags; converts ambiguous columns to explicit names and exposes raw magnitudes for downstream filters and aggregations.

photoobj_spatial_index.name: photoobj_spatial_index
photoobj_spatial_index.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.b,
  p.l
FROM photoobj AS p

semantic_filters.none: no filters; exposes position columns for spatial queries

photoobj_spatial_index.description: Lightweight spatial/proximity-focused projection of photoobj exposing positions and the primary key; useful for spatial joins, neighbor lookups, and filtering by RA/DEC ranges.

photoobj_star_rows.name: photoobj_star_rows
photoobj_star_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.type
FROM photoobj AS p
WHERE p.type = /* STAR_TYPE_VALUE */ 6
  AND p.objid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_rows.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections that are classified as stars by photoobj.type (keeps one row per photometric object). Does not apply magnitude/color cuts — those go in question_ops.

photoobj_magnitudes_canonical.name: photoobj_magnitudes_canonical
photoobj_magnitudes_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  -- positional coords: preserve as double precision (ra/dec already double precision)
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- magnitude columns: explicit NULL handling (use NULLIF to guard against sentinel values if any),
  -- cast to real to ensure consistent type where table might have real
  NULLIF(p.u, 'NaN'::real)   AS u,
  NULLIF(p.g, 'NaN'::real)   AS g,
  NULLIF(p.r, 'NaN'::real)   AS r,
  NULLIF(p.i, 'NaN'::real)   AS i,
  NULLIF(p.z, 'NaN'::real)   AS z,
  -- cmodel magnitudes (preserve as provided, fallback to NULL if NaN)
  NULLIF(p.cmodelmag_u, 'NaN'::real) AS cmodelmag_u,
  NULLIF(p.cmodelmag_g, 'NaN'::real) AS cmodelmag_g,
  NULLIF(p.cmodelmag_r, 'NaN'::real) AS cmodelmag_r,
  -- core positional measures: rowc/colc as real, explicit NULL handling
  NULLIF(p.rowc, 'NaN'::real) AS rowc,
  NULLIF(p.colc, 'NaN'::real) AS colc
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_magnitudes_canonical.description: Normalized projection of photoobj magnitudes and core positional measures (casts/aliases, explicit NULL handling) for reuse in color/magnitude filters and calculations. One row per photoobj.

photo_type_lookup_53.name: photo_type_lookup_53
photo_type_lookup_53.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM photo_type AS pt
photo_type_lookup_53.description: Lookup table mapping photoobj.type integer codes to descriptive names and descriptions. Useful to filter by taxonomy names like 'STAR' instead of numeric literals.

photometric_objects_core.name: photometric_objects_core
photometric_objects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Carry through primary id as object_id
  p.objid AS object_id,
  -- Primary positional columns
  p.ra        AS ra,
  p.dec       AS dec,
  -- Primary magnitude columns (use raw values, exposed under stable names)
  p.u         AS u,
  p.g         AS g,
  p.r         AS r,
  -- Photometric type code (exposed as 'type' to match downstream expectations)
  p.type      AS type
FROM
  -- Prefer to select from the existing canonical photoobj_basic view when available,
  -- falling back to the base table photoobj if not. This body assumes photoobj_basic
  -- exists on the search_path; if not, replace with photoobj.
  photoobj_basic AS p
WHERE
  -- Keep only rows corresponding to a single row per objid (grain requirement).
  -- photoobj_basic is expected to be one row per objid; include a safeguard
  -- to exclude NULL objid if present.
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
photometric_objects_core.description: Canonical cleaned projection of photometric detections with primary positional and magnitude columns, using raw columns as-is but exposing them under stable names for downstream filtering and joins.

photoobj_with_type_label_55.name: photoobj_with_type_label_55
photoobj_with_type_label_55.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS object_id,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS type_name,
  pt.description AS type_description
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_label_55.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined to photo_type to expose human-readable type name/description for each photometric object, enabling type-based filtering (e.g., Galaxy).

photoobj_core_56.name: photoobj_core_56
photoobj_core_56.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- expose native PSF/model magnitudes (keep raw values)
  p.g,
  p.u,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- canonical identifiers of the imaging detection
  p.run,
  p.field,
  -- keep the recorded type and clean flags
  p.type,
  p.clean
FROM
  photoobj p

semantic_filters.no_filters: this view does not apply domain filters; it only projects canonical columns and preserves NULLs

photoobj_core_56.description: Canonical photometric object records with primary identifiers, positions, and native band magnitudes; applies simple null-cleaning (keeps raw values, but exposes presence). Useful as the photometry base for joins and magnitude filters.

specobj_core_57.name: specobj_core_57
specobj_core_57.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.z AS z,
  s.class AS class,
  s.subclass AS subclass,
  s.mjd AS mjd,
  s.plate AS plate,
  s.fiberid AS fiberid
FROM specobj s

semantic_filters.no_filters: this view does not apply domain filters; it only projects canonical spectroscopic columns and preserves NULLs

specobj_core_57.description: Canonical spectroscopic object records with primary identifiers, redshift, classification, and linking field bestobjid for joining to photometric objects. Keeps raw values and NULLs; useful for selecting spectroscopic samples like galaxies and redshift cuts.

photoobj_specobj_join.name: photoobj_specobj_join
photoobj_specobj_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.g,
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.z,
  s.class
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid

semantic_filters.no_filters: the join view does not pre-filter by magnitude or redshift; it only requires the join condition

photoobj_specobj_join.description: Denormalized join of photometric objects to their matching spectroscopic records (via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid). Exposes photometry, positions, spectroscopic redshift and classification in one row per photometric object that has a matched specobj. Designed as a reusable joined cohort for queries that filter photometry by spectroscopic properties.
